Dawon Nexview.why: Its laser micro-bonding systems (pLSMB, 78% of H1 2026 revenue) are the bonding tools MEMS probe-card makers use to build DRAM / NAND wafer-test probe cards; the company says HBM growth adds test steps versus DDR memory and directly benefits its industry, so DRAM / HBM probe-card capacity build-outs drive its orders.
Dawon Nexview.evidence: Dawon Nexview Q2 FY2026 (08-14-2026) half-year report: the company develops, makes and sells the process-automation equipment needed to manufacture probe cards; its Laser Micro-Bonding System bonds 20,000 (NAND) to 100,000 (DRAM) MEMS probe pins onto probe cards, supplied from the world No.1 US probe-card maker to new Chinese and Taiwanese makers.

players.product: laser micro-bonding systems (pLSMB: Laser Micro-Bonding System, High Speed Bonder) for DRAM / NAND MEMS probe-card manufacturing; laser solder-ball jetting repair systems for FC-BGA substrates

Customers above 10% of revenue (not named): Customer 1 KRW 3,943,723 thousand, Customer 2 KRW 1,702,482 thousand, Customer 3 KRW 1,280,850 thousand, Customer 4 KRW 1,199,365 thousand and Customer 5 KRW 1,152,540 thousand of H1 2026 revenue of KRW 11,181,320 thousand (H1 2025 Customer 1: KRW 4,384,550 thousand)

Company view of its market: the DRAM probe-card market, monopolised by US and Japanese makers, is seeing upfront investment for first mass production on the back of Korean makers' localisation, which the company expects to reshape the probe-card market once volume production starts; HBM market growth, driven by AI, autonomous-driving and data-center processors, increases the number of test types versus DDR-based memory, and the company expects its industry to benefit directly. In NAND, domestic new probe-card investment has slowed while China keeps aggressive upfront probe-card investment around its own NAND production. Its Laser Micro-Bonding System bonds 20,000 (NAND) to 100,000 (DRAM) MEMS probe pins at under 60um pitch with 4-5um accuracy, and is supplied from the world No.1 US probe-card maker to new Chinese and Taiwanese makers; it plans to push the DRAM High Speed Bonder and launch a Vertical Pin Inserter for non-memory
quarterly_data.figure: 20,000 to 100,000 probe pins per card; 4-5um accuracy

quarterly_data.signal: Substrate repair (sLSMB): the company says its Laser Solder Ball Jetting batch repair automation equipment was sold to a large Korean company that makes substrates for a leading global CPU company, the world-first mass-production application (company claim), and that it is the only post-reflow / deflux repair tool to pass mass-production verification; it expects large-area FC-BGA substrates for AI CPUs / GPUs, where one missing solder ball among hundreds of thousands can cut yield by over 10%, to drive fast growth of the final-stage micro-bump repair market

Capacity and costs: build-to-order production, so the company cannot state a uniform production capacity; it plans a factory expansion including a cleanroom as orders and sales grow, timing undecided, and moved its head office within Ansan in April 2026. Construction in progress KRW 1,617M; H1 raw-material purchases KRW 7,257M (stages, lasers from suppliers including IPG Photonics Korea and MKS Spectra-Physics); R&D expense KRW 324,317 thousand (2.90% of revenue)
quarterly_data.figure: raw-material purchases KRW 7,257M; R&D KRW 324,317 thousand (2.90%)
